args.title: Knowledge Home Storage
args.content:
Decision (2026-10-05): a project's knowledge home is stored as a field on omp-ui's `ProjectRecord`, not as a key in `<project>/.omp/config.yml`.

Why:
- omp-ui is the only reader. omp never consumes the key, and the repo's rule is that `.omp/config.yml` holds settings omp loads (ADR-0031, ADR-0025). Settings only omp-ui reads live in the registry.
- The value is a machine-local vault path. A project file that may be committed or synced is the wrong place for it.
- Precedent: ADR-0047 (#738) moved the review roster from `REVIEW.yml` files into `ProjectRecord.reviewRoster`.
- No YAML parsing or line-scoped writer edge cases, and no chance of colliding with omp's config schema.

Accepted loss: the setting is not shared through git, and runs outside the app cannot see it.

args.content:
## Partial resolution: where the knowledge home is stored

Decided 2026-10-05. The project's knowledge home is a `ProjectRecord` field in omp-ui's registry. It is not a `.omp/config.yml` key.

Why:

- omp-ui is the only reader. omp never loads this value, and in this repo `.omp/config.yml` holds settings omp itself consumes (ADR-0025, ADR-0031; `CONTEXT.md` says the project layer for subagent models is omp's config file "not a registry field" for exactly that reason). The reverse holds here.
- The value names a vault on this machine. `.omp/` can be committed or synced, and a vault choice from my machine means nothing in someone else's checkout. That is worst for repos the user does not own, which is the case the default rule is meant to serve.
- ADR-0047 as amended by #738 already made this move: the review roster left `REVIEW.yml` for `ProjectRecord.reviewRoster`. `browserClock` is the other precedent. The issue body notes that `ProjectRecord` fields already reach remote instances, which #759 needs.
- No trip through `project-config-writer.ts`, so no refusals on hand-written YAML and no key that could collide with a future omp setting.

Accepted loss: the choice is not shared through git, and sessions started outside the app do not see it. #738 accepted the same trade.

Constraints the field has to carry, from #753:

- Unset is a value distinct from all three choices, so the field is nullable (null = "Not set. The routing default applies.", same convention as `reviewRoster: ReviewDocument | null`).
- The `vault` and `both` choices need room for a vault reference, and that reference also needs a "follow the default write vault" state if pin-versus-follow goes that way.

Still open on this ticket: the default rule, pin versus follow, what `both` writes, whether a Session-scope override exists, how the agent learns the rule, and the write guidance. Leaving the ticket open.

finalAssistantText:
The `ProjectRecord` choice is now on the record. There's no code to write yet: the design plan (#749) is planning-only, and implementation starts only after its final spec ticket, #762, closes.

**Where I recorded it:**
- **Issue [#756](https://github.com/LankfordAI/omp-ui/issues/756#issuecomment-6004578052)** is the open ticket that asks this storage question, so I posted the decision there as a partial resolution. The comment covers why we chose the field and what we give up.
- **Vault note** [[omp-ui/Knowledge Home Storage|Knowledge Home Storage]] now has a confirmation line that links to that comment.

**What the field needs to hold**, based on the #753 prototype:
- An empty value for "not set". That's a real fourth state alongside Repo docs, Vault and Both, and it means the routing default applies. `reviewRoster: ReviewDocument | null` already works this way.
- A slot that says which vault the Vault and Both choices mean. It may also need a "follow the default write vault" setting, depending on how one of the open questions below is decided.

**I left #756 open.** These parts of it are still undecided:
- the default rule when the user hasn't chosen
- whether a project's vault stays fixed or follows the default write vault
- what Both actually writes
- whether a session can override the project's choice
- how the agent learns the rule
- what the agent is told to write

The design plan says to close a ticket only once it's fully answered, and to add its one-line summary to the plan at that point. So I haven't added anything to #749.
